home.listenDescription: 60 seconds of therapeutic tone to calm the vestibular system before your journey.
home.motionCuesDescription: Eight breathing dots at the screen edges follow your vehicle's motion — reconciling sight and sense.
home.researchNote: Based on research from Nagoya University (2025) and Apple's Vehicle Motion Cues.
home.welcomeBody: A 60-second 100 Hz audio session and on-screen motion cues that may help reduce motion sickness symptoms during travel.

audio.title: Audio Therapy
audio.volumeGuide: Put on headphones and set volume to a comfortable level.
audio.volumeTip: The sound should be clearly audible but never uncomfortable.
audio.whyExplainer: A pure 100 Hz tone may help calm the vestibular system — the inner-ear organ behind motion sickness.
audio.interrupted: Session paused — the audio was interrupted.
audio.errorHint: Check your volume and try again.

done.title: All Done
done.message: Your 100 Hz session is complete. Take a breath and start your journey.
done.disclaimer: Results may vary by individual. Based on research from Nagoya University.

motionCues.title: Motion Cues
motionCues.howItWorks: 8 subtle dots on your screen edges move with your vehicle's motion, helping your brain reconcile what your eyes see with what your body feels.

tips.title: Get the best results
tips.subtitle: Small habits that make the cues work harder for you.
tips.tip1: Turn on the cues before the ride starts — prevention beats reaction.
tips.tip2: Keep your phone where you can see it, ideally mounted or held steady.
tips.tip3: Pair with the 100 Hz audio session for sound and visual relief.
tips.tip4: Still feeling unwell? Look at the horizon and rest your eyes off the screen.
tips.disclaimer: Serene may help reduce motion sickness symptoms — results vary from person to person.

help.q1: The dots don't appear over other apps
help.a1: Check that "Display over other apps" is granted, then stop and start the overlay again.
help.q2: The dots freeze or disappear after a while
help.a2: Battery optimization may be stopping the service. In Settings → Battery, set Serene to Unrestricted (names vary by device).
help.q3: Why is there a persistent notification?
help.a3: Android requires a notification while an overlay service runs. It's set to minimum importance — silent and collapsed.
help.q4: The settings screen looks different on my device
help.a4: On Android 11 and newer, the system opens a list of all apps — find Serene there. On older versions it opens Serene's page directly. Manufacturer skins may rename the setting.

onboarding.slide1Description: We'll walk you through enabling it in seconds.
onboarding.slide2Tip: Tip: You can also add it to Control Center for quick toggling.
onboarding.slide3Subtitle: We'll open the Accessibility settings directly for you.

control.appleCuesDescription: Works across all apps, even when Serene is closed
control.inAppDescription: Show dots while using Serene (foreground only)
control.unsupportedVersion: This feature requires iOS 18 or later. Please update your iPhone.
control.openSettingsFallback: Open Settings → Accessibility → Motion → Vehicle Motion Cues manually.

help.q1: I can't find Vehicle Motion Cues
help.a1: It requires iOS 18 or later on iPhone 12 and newer. Update iOS in Settings → General → Software Update, then look under Accessibility → Motion.
help.a2: Settings → Accessibility → Motion → Vehicle Motion Cues. Choose Automatic so your iPhone shows the dots only while you're in a moving vehicle.
help.q3: Why does Serene's overlay only work inside the app?
help.a3: Apple doesn't allow third-party apps to draw over other apps. For system-wide dots, use Apple's built-in Vehicle Motion Cues.
